es: Valorar una actuación oral modelo con una rúbrica de cuatro criterios: estructura, precisión, tacto y evidencia.

teaching.en: A rubric sets out the criteria by which we assess a performance, so that a verdict rests on evidence rather than on mood.
teaching.es: Una rúbrica establece los criterios con los que valoramos una actuación, de modo que el veredicto se apoye en pruebas y no en el estado de ánimo.
teaching.explanationEs: Valorar con criterios evita las impresiones vagas del tipo «me gustó» o «me aburrió».
segments: A rubric sets out the criteria by which we assess a performance,
so that a verdict rests on evidence rather than on mood.
teaching.audioText: A rubric sets out the criteria by which we assess a performance, so that a verdict rests on evidence rather than on mood.

teaching.en: The first criterion is structure: a coherent talk opens with a clear purpose, develops two or three reasons in order, and closes by drawing them together.
teaching.es: El primer criterio es la estructura: una charla coherente abre con un propósito claro, desarrolla dos o tres razones en orden y cierra reuniéndolas.
teaching.explanationEs: Se comprueba con las señales de orden: first, second, finally, to sum up.
segments: The first criterion is structure: a coherent talk opens with a clear purpose,
develops two or three reasons in order, and closes by drawing them together.
teaching.audioText: The first criterion is structure: a coherent talk opens with a clear purpose, develops two or three reasons in order, and closes by drawing them together.

teaching.en: The second criterion is accuracy, and any shortcoming here, such as a slip in tense or a misused connector, is judged by how far it blurs the message.
teaching.es: El segundo criterio es la precisión, y cualquier defecto aquí, como un desliz de tiempo o un conector mal usado, se juzga según cuánto difumina el mensaje.
teaching.explanationEs: Un error que no impide entender pesa menos que uno que cambia el sentido.
segments: The second criterion is accuracy, and any shortcoming here, such as a slip in
tense or a misused connector, is judged by how far it blurs the message.
teaching.audioText: The second criterion is accuracy, and any shortcoming here, such as a slip in tense or a misused connector, is judged by how far it blurs the message.

teaching.en: Tact is the third: a skilled speaker concedes a point and softens a request, and does not digress into blame or complaint.
teaching.es: El tacto es el tercero: quien habla con habilidad concede un punto y suaviza una petición, y no se desvía hacia el reproche o la queja.
teaching.explanationEs: Much as…, I was wondering whether… y should it fail son señales de tacto.
segments: Tact is the third: a skilled speaker concedes a point and
softens a request, and does not digress into blame or complaint.
teaching.audioText: Tact is the third: a skilled speaker concedes a point and softens a request, and does not digress into blame or complaint.

teaching.en: The fourth criterion is evidence: a speaker who can cite a survey, a figure or a precise example is harder to ignore than one who says that many people agree.
teaching.es: El cuarto criterio es la evidencia: quien puede citar una encuesta, una cifra o un ejemplo preciso es más difícil de ignorar que quien dice que mucha gente está de acuerdo.
teaching.explanationEs: Una encuesta, una cifra o un ejemplo concreto valen más que «todo el mundo lo piensa».
segments: The fourth criterion is evidence: a speaker who can cite a survey, a figure or
a precise example is harder to ignore than one who says that many people agree.
teaching.audioText: The fourth criterion is evidence: a speaker who can cite a survey, a figure or a precise example is harder to ignore than one who says that many people agree.

teaching.en: A fair verdict names a strength and a weakness, and it quotes the exact words that prove each one.
teaching.es: Un veredicto justo nombra una fortaleza y una debilidad, y cita las palabras exactas que prueban cada una.
teaching.explanationEs: Sin la cita exacta, una valoración es solo una opinión.
segments: A fair verdict names a strength and a weakness, and
it quotes the exact words that prove each one.
teaching.audioText: A fair verdict names a strength and a weakness, and it quotes the exact words that prove each one.

prompt.es: ¿Qué criterio se aprecia sobre todo en esta apertura y este cierre?

choices.text: Tact: it softens a difficult request for the audience.
Evidence: it backs each reason with figures and examples.
Structure: it frames the talk and draws it together.

feedback.es: Una apertura que anuncia la propuesta y un cierre que reúne las razones ordenan el discurso: es estructura, no tacto ni datos.

hint.es: Apertura y cierre ordenan el discurso; no suavizan peticiones ni aportan cifras.

origin.text: Opening: Tonight I want to make one proposal and support it with two reasons. Closing: So, to draw these threads together, a night bus would serve workers, cost little and deserve a trial.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quien puede citar una encuesta o una cifra es más difícil de ignorar.»

feedback.es: Cite a survey es la colocación habitual para apoyar una razón con una fuente concreta.

hint.es: Verbo que significa mencionar una fuente o un dato como prueba.

origin.text: A speaker who can ___ a survey, a figure or a precise example is harder to ignore than one who says that many people agree.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Su estructura es coherente, pero su evidencia es débil.»

answer.text: Her structure is coherent but her evidence is weak

feedback.es: La frase contrapone una fortaleza y una debilidad, cada una con su criterio.

hint.es: Empieza por el criterio que funciona y deja la debilidad para el final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué criterio demuestra sobre todo este fragmento de la charla.

choices.text: Tact: she recognises other views and keeps a way back open.
Structure: she sets out her reasons in a clear order.
Accuracy: she repairs a wrong verb form as she goes.

feedback.es: Reconoce a quienes piensan distinto («I respect that»), pide con una pregunta indirecta («might I ask whether») y deja una salida: todo ello es tacto.

origin.audio: I realise that some of you would rather keep the quiet hours as they are, and I respect that. Even so, might I ask whether the library could open one evening a week for students with exams? If the experiment does not work, we can simply return to the old timetable.

prompt.es: ¿Qué criterio demuestra esta parte de la charla y por qué?

choices.text: Structure, since it opens and closes the talk clearly.
Evidence, since it offers a figure and a comparison.
Tact, since it acknowledges the staff's worries about cost.

feedback.es: Una encuesta con una cifra y el caso de un colegio vecino son datos concretos: el criterio es evidencia.

origin.text: According to a survey of four hundred students, nearly two thirds revise after eight in the evening. The school down the road opened its library on Friday nights two years ago, and attendance has doubled.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada cita de una charla con el criterio o el defecto que ilustra.

pairs: First, I propose a night bus; second, a trial; finally, a review.
Much as I appreciate the concern, I would ask for a trial.
A survey of two hundred students shows that most study at night.
She had went to the council last week.
…which brings me, rather abruptly, to my holiday.

feedback.es: Cada cita deja una señal observable: orden, cortesía, datos, un error de forma o una digresión.

pairs: First, I propose a night bus; second, a trial; finally, a review.
Much as I appreciate the concern, I would ask for a trial.
A survey of two hundred students shows that most study at night.
She had went to the council last week.
…which brings me, rather abruptly, to my holiday.

prompt.es: Escucha la charla y elige la actitud de la oradora ante la objeción del municipio.

choices.text: She brushes it aside as exaggerated and unimportant.
She agrees that a pilot route would be too costly.
She takes it seriously and proposes a limited trial.

feedback.es: Reconoce la preocupación con «Much as I appreciate» y responde con un ensayo de tres meses: toma en serio la objeción sin ceder.

origin.audio: I would like to argue that our town needs a night bus. First, a survey of three hundred residents shows that many workers finish after midnight and cannot get home safely. Second, two neighbouring towns introduced a night route last year, and in both cases more people used it than the forecasts had predicted. Much as I appreciate the council's concern about costs, a pilot route would be modest. I was wondering whether we might try it for three months. Should it fail, we will stop. To sum up, a small experiment could spare hundreds of people a dangerous walk home.

prompt.es: ¿Qué criterio falla con más claridad en esta intervención?

choices.text: Tact, because it issues demands and closes the debate.
Structure, because its points follow no clear order.
Accuracy, because several verb forms are wrong.

feedback.es: El orden es claro (first, second, third), pero exigir y negarse a escuchar cierra el debate: falla el tacto.

origin.text: First, I would like to propose a night bus. Second, you must pay for it, and I will not listen to objections. Third, everybody knows that buses are good, so there is nothing more to discuss. Finally, thank you.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su único defecto real fue la falta de evidencia; lo demás, bien resuelto.»

feedback.es: Shortcoming designa una carencia puntual dentro de un conjunto positivo, justo lo que describe la frase.

origin.text: The talk was clear, polite and well ordered. Her one real ___ was the lack of evidence; everything else was handled with skill.

prompt.es: Valora la intervención: una fortaleza y una debilidad, con evidencia citada.

answer.text: One strength is the structure, because she says first, second and finally. One weakness is the evidence, because she cites no survey and no figure.
accepted: One strength is the structure, because she says first, second and finally. One weakness is the evidence, because she cites no survey and no figure.
Her main strength is tact, because she says I was wondering whether the council might try it. Her weakness is the lack of evidence, because there is no survey.
One strength is that the talk is clearly ordered, with first, second and finally. One shortcoming is that she gives no evidence, so her reasons are weak.

feedback.es: Una valoración completa nombra una fortaleza y una debilidad y cita la frase exacta que demuestra cada una.

origin.text: First, I would like to propose a night bus. Second, a pilot route would be cheap. Finally, I was wondering whether the council might try it. There is no survey and no figure to support any of this, although everything is clearly ordered.

evidenceGroups: a pilot route would be cheap

prompt.es: ¿Qué opina en realidad el evaluador de la intervención que describe?

choices.text: Weak in form although persuasive in content and in argument.
Both polished and convincing, but rather boring to hear.
Poorly prepared, because it wandered far from its subject.
Polished in form but not convincing for lack of support.

feedback.es: Elogia la forma (tidy, calm) pero ninguna afirmación tiene apoyo y nunca convence: pulida, pero sin fuerza argumental.

origin.text: The talk was tidy and the delivery was calm, yet I left without a single reason to change my mind. Every claim was plausible; none was supported. The speaker never digressed, never hesitated and never convinced me. It was a nice talk that gave me nothing to disagree with and nothing to believe.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Un veredicto justo cita las palabras exactas que lo demuestran.»

answer.text: A fair verdict quotes the exact words that prove it

feedback.es: Quotes the exact words vincula la valoración con una evidencia verificable.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una charla que se desvía de su propósito no es coherente.»

feedback.es: Coherent describe un discurso cuyas partes se apoyan entre sí; si las razones no se enlazan, no lo es.

origin.text: A talk that keeps drifting away from its purpose is not ___: its reasons never build on one another.
